To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optical spectra of InAs/ InP QWrs and QWs show unusual temperature dependences, which are explained in terms of thermodynamic activation of excitonic states, and that the room temperature spectra of QWrs are modified by a change of their dimensionality from 1D into anisotropic 3D.
the temperature dependence of the PL of InAs/ InP quantum wires is characterized by two-branch switching.
the temperature dependence of the excitonic ground state energies and the dimensionality of the InAs/Inp quantum wires can be controlled by the thickness of the InAs quantum well.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the electronic and optical properties of shallow InAs quantum wires grown by molecular beam epitaxy on InP(001) substrates and their parent quantum wells.
the investigation of optical properties of InP/InAs QWr nanostructures and their parent InP/InGaAs quantum well systems.
the optical properties of shallow InAs QWr nanostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the observed phenomena are a result of the thermal activation process, which is a direct manifestation of the 1D character of the nanostructures.

the PL spectra of QWr and well samples show a two-branch switching, which can be interpreted as a thermal activation of exciton states, whereas the absorbance spectra of QWr samples show a strong modification of the line shape, which can be explained by a thermal induced change of the system dimensionality.
the PL of the InAs/InGaP(001) QWrs is governed by the interplay of the dimensionality and thermal activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the existence of a new type of 1D-2D crossover in the temperature dependence of the optical properties for the InAs/Inp QWr nanostructures.
the InAs/InAsP/InP(100) system is a very promising material for the fabrication of low-dimensional nanostructures.
the InAs/InAs QWr system exhibits the same type of excitonic properties as InAs/InGaAs QWr systems, which are well known to be very promising for optoelectronic device applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PL and FTIR measurements are powerful tools for the investigation of the optical characteristics of InAs/ InP QWrs and QWls.
the optical properties of QWr samples are strongly influenced by the dimensionality of their parent QWs.
the temperature induced change in the dimensionality of the nanostructures is an important factor to be accounted for when studying and interpreting the optical properties of nanostructures.
